purpose: Independent simulated beginner mouse-only usability report based on visible RILL actions and screenshots.
persona: Simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a short hip-hop beat with a simple synth part.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible MIDI creation prompt, direct note drawing, instrument assignment and mouse keyboard enabled the full task. Exact trimming and Duplicate behavior required small corrections.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Clean dark interface with coordinated teal clips, readable waveforms and note previews; sparse enough to follow. The many similar narrow repeated clips are visually repetitive and their names become truncated.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most clicks and note edits gave immediate visible feedback. Playback briefly prepared audio and WAV export took several seconds before a clear completion notice. Screenshot/tool overhead is not an app speed benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Mostly clear labels, but context-menu Duplicate immediately copied while toolbar Duplicate selected a tool. A small edge drag did not correct the trim until coarser snapping was used; stopping playback also dismissed rename mode.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The requested audio arrangement, VST instrument, mouse-drawn MIDI, naming, project save, WAV and MIDI exports were all available. This narrow session does not establish broader production or third-party plug-in completeness.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the labeled empty MIDI area opened the instrument library; Assign instrument created the track and clip with Rill Lab Sine displayed.
Pencil drags created a visible four-note motif with labeled notes and velocity stems.
Context-menu Duplicate immediately created a neighboring MIDI clip. Clicking toolbar Duplicate twice did not add clips; it selected a mode whose help text required clicking a clip.
The first audio trim produced 30.134 seconds and a tiny corrective drag left it unchanged. Selecting 1-bar snapping and dragging again produced the visible 30.000-second end.
After a Preparing audio state, playback advanced the playhead and transport position, with visible activity in the audio and instrument track meters.
Stopping playback while project rename controls were open dismissed those controls; reopening Rename project restored access to the keyboard.
The on-screen keyboard accepted a mouse-entered name. Save and both export dialogs automatically proposed filenames using that name.
WAV export displayed an arrangement length summary and an effect-tails toggle. WAV and MIDI exports both showed explicit Exported notices.
The immediate first save screenshot contained a black rectangle over the dialog area; the next screenshot showed a readable native save dialog without intervention.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: named and saved the project, arranged audio and VST MIDI to a displayed 30.000 seconds, and saw success notices for both exports. File contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4; supplied Circuit rhythm audio duplicated into three full four-bar clips and a final two-bar trim, with a one-bar C4/D#4/G4/F4 MIDI motif repeated across 14 bars. Intended as a simple beat with synth part; sound and stylistic success were not auditioned.
outcome.playback_observed: Play changed to Pause, initially showed Preparing audio, then the playhead and transport advanced to approximately bar 7 with both tracks' meters active. Stopped and returned to the beginning before save/export.

limitations: No file contents or heard audio claim; independent coordinator verification follows.
Used only assigned session screenshots and mouse driver for composition and app operation; reports were written separately as allowed.
Laboratory software graphics and virtual audio sink; observed speed and meters are not physical hardware latency or audio quality measurements.
One supplied native VST3 instrument was tested; no conclusion about other third-party plug-ins.
Used supplied startup audio; the result is a repetitive beginner arrangement and was not auditioned to assess hip-hop style or musical quality.
